summary.title: How to implement a programming language in JavaScript
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a small Lisp-like language in JavaScript, covering parsing, an interpreter, continuations, and a compiler.
keywords: why not use regexps to parse code
takeaways: Parsing is covered first, with the advice to avoid regexps for parsing programming languages.
You write an interpreter for the λanguage, a language with infix syntax and power similar to Scheme but without macros.
Continuations are explained, including why they matter.
A compiler is written, and code is transformed to continuation-passing style, with a few basic optimizations.
summary.summary: This tutorial walks through implementing a programming language in JavaScript/NodeJS, aimed at the average JavaScript programmer. It proceeds in a simple-to-advanced order: a parser, an interpreter, continuations, then a compiler with continuation-passing style transformation and basic optimizations. The language built, called λanguage, uses classical infix syntax rather than Lisp syntax and is said to be about as powerful as Scheme, minus macros. The excerpt shown is only the introduction and outline, so the implementation details are not visible here.
